method: All URLs verified on 2026-09-19 with curl HEAD (or a 4-byte ranged GET where HEAD is not honoured); no full artifact was downloaded. content_length is the Content-Length reported by the final 200/206 response. ZIP top-level listings were read from the ZIP central directory via ranged GETs; 7z contents were not inspected (7z headers are not readable without the whole file).

apps.extraction_notes: OBSERVED from the central directory: 3134 entries / 2484 files, ~1.046 GB uncompressed. No single wrapping folder: the root holds Code.exe, Code.VisualElementsManifest.xml, bin/, policies/, tools/, appx/ and a commit-named folder `7debcd0e2a/` that holds 3092 of the entries (the application resources). apps.name: Wireshark
apps.license_source: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/raw/master/COPYING (GPL version 2, June 1991); Wireshark states 'GPLv2 or later' in its README/about

artifact.sha256_source: https://www.wireshark.org/download/SIGNATURES-4.6.8.txt, line 'SHA256(Wireshark-4.6.8-x64.exe)=8eba737c...' (file also states 98934936 bytes, matching Content-Length)

apps.extraction_notes: NSIS installer, SetCompressor /SOLID lzma with 64 MB dictionary (packaging/nsis/wireshark.nsi lines 10-11 on branch release-4.6). 7-Zip can list/extract it (`7z x`), but the payload INCLUDES third-party dependency installers that are not application files: `npcap-<ver>.exe` and `USBPcapSetup-<ver>.exe` are embedded via `File` directives (wireshark.nsi lines 916 and 927, branch release-4.6). Exclude those two files (and the NSIS $PLUGINSDIR content) when measuring the application tree. The alternative host https://www.wireshark.org/download/win64/Wireshark-4.6.8-x64.exe serves the same Content-Length.
apps.alternatives_considered: No official plain zip/7z exists. WiresharkPortable64_4.6.8.paf.exe (109359568 bytes, sha256 d6cf5056586a0156c8634a9d9b3097e60a8dda408b889c9afc4445ec2b18d581) is a PortableApps.com NSIS package (adds the PortableApps launcher and, per PortableApps convention, still bundles Npcap), so it is not cleaner than the installer. Wireshark-4.6.8-x64.msi (81874944 bytes, sha256 779ee66f846376942a3b631a78bba8c3d509697d07743349e1893056211d05e3) is the MSI variant.

apps.name: GIMP
apps.license_source: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gimp/-/raw/master/COPYING (GPL version 3); the '-or-later' is the project's stated licence (GPLv3+) and was not re-verified from a per-file header here
apps.release_page: https://www.gimp.org/downloads/ ('The current stable release of GIMP is 3.2.6 (2026-09-10)'); directory https://download.gimp.org/gimp/v3.2/windows/ (marker file 0.0_LATEST-IS-3.2.6)

artifact.sha256_source: https://download.gimp.org/gimp/v3.2/windows/SHA256SUMS (line '9337cccb...  gimp-3.2.6-setup.exe'); SHA512SUMS in the same directory gives bc5fa3cd...f97ca

apps.extraction_notes: Inno Setup installer. download.gimp.org answers 302 to a mirror (observed: https://mirrors.ukfast.co.uk/sites/gimp.org/pub/gimp/v3.2/windows/gimp-3.2.6-setup.exe, 200, Content-Length 190358080); the mirror choice may vary, the bytes should not -- verify against the SHA256SUMS. The installer is a UNIVERSAL x64 + ARM64 package (gimp.org: 'for x86_64 and ARM64'; gimp-setup.iss defines ARCHS_INSTALLED="x64os arm64" when both bundles are present), so innoextract will yield both architecture trees; count only the x64 tree. GIMP's build script downloads the LATEST Inno Setup release at build time (3_dist-gimp-inno.ps1 line 30 queries jrsoftware/issrc releases/latest), so the Inno Setup format version is recent (6.5/7.x era); innoextract compatibility with that format version is NOT established and must be checked with `innoextract --info` before relying on it.
apps.alternatives_considered: No official portable zip/7z for Windows. The MSIX (Microsoft Store) build exists but is a Store artifact. v3.0 directory (gimp-3.0.8-setup-2.exe) is the previous series, not current.

apps.name: WinSCP
apps.license_source: https://winscp.net/eng/docs/license ('GNU General Public License (GPL) ... either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version')
apps.extraction_notes: OBSERVED from the central directory: 4 files at the root, no folder -- WinSCP.exe, WinSCP.com, license.txt, readme.txt (24389189 bytes uncompressed). Acquisition caveat (OBSERVED): the SourceForge URL serves the ZIP bytes (302 -> downloads.sourceforge.net -> <mirror>.dl.sourceforge.net, 206 with a signed fid/e/st token, body starts with PK) ONLY when the client sends a non-browser User-Agent (curl default UA and 'Wget/1.21' both work); with a 'Mozilla/5.0' UA every SourceForge host, including downloads.sourceforge.net and master.dl.sourceforge.net, returns the HTML landing page (200 text/html). winscp.net's own direct link (https://winscp.net/download/files/<date+token>/WinSCP-6.5.7-Portable.zip, 200, 8801298 bytes) and the CDN link (https://cdn.winscp.net/files/WinSCP-6.5.7-Portable.zip?secure=...) carry per-request tokens and are not stable URLs; https://cdn.winscp.net/files/WinSCP-6.5.7-Portable.zip without the token is 403. The winget manifest for WinSCP.WinSCP 6.5.6 uses the same sourceforge.net/.../download URL pattern (InstallerUrl), which supports its use as the reproducible URL.
apps.alternatives_considered: WinSCP-6.5.7-Setup.exe (Inno Setup) and WinSCP-6.5.7.msi (WiX) carry the same executables plus installer glue. WinSCP-6.6.3.RC-Portable.zip and the x64-Experimental portable are release candidates, not stable. NOTE: the stable 6.5.7 portable is the 32-bit (x86) build -- the x64 build exists only as '6.6.3.RC-Portable-x64-Experimental'; WinSCP's stable line ships no x64 binary.

apps.extraction_notes: The gallery link https://inkscape.org/gallery/item/59503/inkscape-1.4.4_2026-05-05_dcaf3e7-x64_mHK170m.7z redirects (observed 200 at the media URL above); https://media.inkscape.org/media/resources/file/<same name> also answers 200 with the same Content-Length. INFERENCE: the '_mHK170m' / '_BKqiyKW' suffixes are the site's storage de-duplication suffixes, and the .sha256 file (named for the un-suffixed filename) describes these same bytes -- confirm by hashing after download. INFERENCE (not inspected): the 7z unpacks to a single top-level folder `inkscape/` containing bin/, lib/, share/, etc. inkscape.org returned intermittent HTTP 502 during this session; retry on 502.
apps.alternatives_considered: inkscape-1.4.4_2026-05-05_dcaf3e7-x64.signed.exe (NSIS installer, sha256 file at .../sigs/inkscape-1.4.4_2026-05-05_dcaf3e7-x64.signed.exe.sha256) and the .signed.msi (WiX). The 7z is the unsigned raw tree and was preferred per the brief.
